intro.text: Designer Brands is one of the world's largest designers, producers, and retailers of the most recognizable footwear brands and accessories, transforming and defining the footwear industry through a mission of being shoe obsessed. With a diversified, world-class portfolio of coveted brands, including Topo Athletic, Keds, Vince Camuto, Kelly & Katie, Jessica Simpson, Lucky Brand, Mix No. 6, Crown Vintage and others, Designer Brands designs and produces on-trend footwear and accessories for all of life's occasions delivered to the consumer through a robust direct-to-consumer omni-channel infrastructure and powerful national wholesale distribution.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

The ultimate impact of tariffs and other trade policies on our business will depend on several factors, including future measures implemented by the U.S. government and the governments of other countries, the overall magnitude and duration of these measures, and our ability to mitigate effects, which could include higher import costs and our ability to obtain any refund.
Our success depends on our ability to remain competitive with respect to assortment, fashion trends, quality, convenience, and value.
We rely on our strong relationships with our suppliers.

The success of our business depends on our ability to obtain products from our suppliers, including national brand suppliers and third-party manufacturers, on a timely basis, on acceptable terms, and to our specifications.
The loss of any of our major suppliers could disrupt our operations and adversely affect our business.
The loss of, or a reduction in the amount and quality of merchandise supplied by, any of our high-volume suppliers could have an adverse effect on our business.

Our operating results depend on the orderly operation of our receiving, distribution, and fulfillment processes, which in turn depend on suppliers' adherence to shipping schedules and our effective management of our facilities.
We rely on the flow of goods through ports worldwide on a consistent basis from factories and suppliers.
We rely on third parties to provide customer payment processing services.

Our business relies on IT networks and systems to market and sell our products, process financial and personal information, manage a variety of business processes, and comply with regulatory, legal, and tax requirements.

We also depend on a variety of information systems to effectively process customer orders and other data, for digital marketing activities, and for electronic communications with our associates, customers, prospective customers, and vendors.

We rely on associates, contractors, and other third parties who may attempt to circumvent our security measures in order to obtain personal information or other sensitive data and may purposefully or inadvertently cause a breach involving such information.
We rely on our ability to retain and maintain good relationships with the licensors and their ability to maintain strong, well-recognized brands and trademarks.

The demand for the brands we sell may also depend on how we are viewed relative to corporate social responsibility ("CSR"), including environmental, social, and governance positions, which may not align with the expectations of our customers, investors, and other stakeholders.

We are dependent on our retail customer reward programs and marketing to drive traffic, sales, and loyalty, and any decrease in membership or purchases from members could have a material adverse effect on our business.

We rely on our reward programs to drive customer traffic, sales, and purchase frequency as members earn points toward discounts on future purchases through our VIP reward programs in the U.S. and Canada.

Our ability to operate stores on a profitable basis depends on many factors, including our ability to identify suitable markets and sites for our store locations with financially stable co-tenants and landlords; build-out or remodel sites on a timely and effective basis; obtain sufficient financing and capital resources or generate sufficient cash flows from operations to fund store capital expenditures; open new stores or remodel existing stores at costs not significantly greater than those anticipated; successfully open new stores in markets in which we currently have few or no stores; contr
Such estimates rely on the completeness of recorded markdowns.
